title: Browser Bridge Stability — Offscreen Document migration
description: Implement the approved plan at .omc/plans/browser-bridge-stability.md (rev 2). Move the WebSocket from the MV3 service worker into a Chrome Offscreen Document with a long-lived chrome.runtime.connect port for offscreen↔SW RPC, and debounce the Python-side lonely-watcher pair-code regeneration. Fixes the 10-second connect/disconnect cycle.

stories.title: Create offscreen.js — WebSocket owner with port-based RPC forwarding
stories.description: Move all WebSocket lifecycle (connect, auth/pair handshake, pong-check, reconnect/backoff) from background.js into offscreen.js. Open a long-lived chrome.runtime.connect port to the SW with name 'heare-rpc'. Forward daemon RPC requests to the SW via port.postMessage and resolve pending Promises on port.onMessage. Forward connection-state changes to the SW for badge updates. Reconnect the port on onDisconnect.
acceptanceCriteria: extensions/heare-bridge/offscreen.js exists
File defines `let swPort = null` and a `pendingRPCs` Map for in-flight RPC tracking
File defines `connectPort()` that calls `chrome.runtime.connect({name: 'heare-rpc'})` and reconnects on `onDisconnect` after a short setTimeout delay
File defines `sendRPCToSW(id, method, params)` returning a Promise; rejected via setTimeout on RPC timeout (>= 30s)
WebSocket constants DEFAULT_PORT, BACKOFF_STEPS, PONG_TIMEOUT_MS are present in this file (no longer in background.js)
`ws.onopen` sends auth or pair handshake via JSON.stringify({v:1, type:'auth'|'pair', ...})
`ws.onmessage` handles 'auth_result', 'pair_result', 'pong', and 'request' message types from the daemon
On daemon `request`, the handler calls `sendRPCToSW(id, method, params)` and writes the resolved {ok,result/error} back to the WS as `{v:1, id, type:'response', ...}`
Connection-state transitions (connected/auth_failed/pair_failed/disconnected) are forwarded to the SW via `swPort.postMessage({type:'connection_state', state:...})`
Successful pairing forwards token to SW via `swPort.postMessage({type:'pair_success', token})`
`pong` messages from the daemon update `lastPongTime`; the in-offscreen pong-check setInterval triggers reconnect if PONG_TIMEOUT_MS exceeded

stories.title: background.js: refactor SW into thin RPC + ensureOffscreen proxy
stories.description: Remove WebSocket lifecycle from background.js. Keep all 7 RPC handlers (list_tabs, read_page, click, fill, extract, navigate, open_tab) plus HANDLERS map and badge helpers. Add `ensureOffscreen()` with try/catch + HAS_OFFSCREEN fallback (M3). Add `chrome.runtime.onConnect` listener for the 'heare-rpc' port that dispatches rpc_request to HANDLERS, returns rpc_response, updates badge on connection_state, and stores pair_success token. Replace the existing reconnect message-loop bug (M2) by forwarding popup/options reconnect to offscreen via the port, never via sendMessage re-broadcast.
acceptanceCriteria: extensions/heare-bridge/background.js no longer defines `let ws`, `connect()`, `disconnect()`, `scheduleReconnect()`, `startPongCheck()`, `stopPongCheck()`, or `loadConfig()` at module scope (these moved to offscreen.js)
All 7 RPC handler functions (handleListTabs, handleReadPage, handleClick, handleFill, handleExtract, handleNavigate, handleOpenTab) and HANDLERS map remain present
Badge helpers badgeGreen, badgeRed, badgePairFailed, badgeGrey remain present
File defines `let HAS_OFFSCREEN = typeof chrome.offscreen !== 'undefined'` (let, not const, for M3 fallback)

File defines `async function ensureOffscreen()` that wraps `chrome.offscreen.hasDocument()` + `chrome.offscreen.createDocument({url:'offscreen.html', reasons:[chrome.offscreen.Reason.WORKERS], justification:...})` in try/catch and sets HAS_OFFSCREEN=false on error
No occurrence of `chrome.offscreen.Reason.WEB_RTC` anywhere in background.js (S4)

`chrome.runtime.onConnect.addListener` registers a listener that filters by `port.name === 'heare-rpc'`, stores `offscreenPort`, dispatches `rpc_request` to HANDLERS, returns `rpc_response` via `port.postMessage`, updates badge on `connection_state`, and stores token on `pair_success`

`chrome.runtime.onMessage` listener for `{type:'reconnect'}` forwards via `offscreenPort.postMessage({type:'reconnect'})` — does NOT call `chrome.runtime.sendMessage({type:'reconnect'})` (no self-delivery loop)
onInstalled and onStartup lifecycle listeners call `ensureOffscreen()` (and fall back to legacy `connect()` only when `HAS_OFFSCREEN === false`)
Existing `chrome.alarms.create('keepalive', {periodInMinutes: 0.4})` is preserved as belt-and-suspenders

stories.title: Tests: add fast debounce test (S5) and rapid-cycling test
stories.description: Two new tests in tests/test_browser_bridge.py. The debounce test monkey-patches PAIR_CODE_REGEN_AFTER_LONELY_S to 2.0 to keep CI fast (<5s total).
acceptanceCriteria: tests/test_browser_bridge.py defines `test_lonely_watcher_debounce` that monkey-patches `src.agent.browser_bridge.PAIR_CODE_REGEN_AFTER_LONELY_S` to 2.0, asserts no pair code is generated within 1s of disconnect, and asserts a new pair code IS generated by ~2.5s after disconnect
tests/test_browser_bridge.py defines `test_rapid_cycling_no_pair_codes` that connects/disconnects 5 times in a loop with ~1s gaps and asserts no pair code was minted during the cycling
Both new tests pass under `uv run pytest tests/test_browser_bridge.py::test_lonely_watcher_debounce tests/test_browser_bridge.py::test_rapid_cycling_no_pair_codes -v`
Combined runtime of both new tests is < 10 seconds
